bypass_options.notes: Saudi Arabia: Persian Gulf fields to Yanbu on the Red Sea. Only carries Saudi crude; near-zero extra transit time since it was headed toward Red Sea/Suez shipping lanes anyway. Estimate.
UAE: Habshan fields to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, entirely outside Hormuz. Near-zero extra transit time. Estimate.

No pipeline exists for Iranian (Kharg Island) or Qatari (Ras Laffan) crude -- only option is sailing around Africa instead of through Hormuz. Unlimited capacity (any tanker can do it) but adds ~10-14 days transit for Persian Gulf-to-Europe/Americas routes. Estimate.

explanation: 6,190,000 bpd depends on hormuz. Pipeline/alternate-strait bypasses (Petroline (East-West Pipeline), ADCOP (Abu Dhabi Crude Oil Pipeline)) can absorb all of it with little to no added transit time.
